artboards.title: A · Worktree is the card (not chosen)
C · Folder card, branch on the row (not chosen)

annotations.text:
Top: the trip, with the taps drawn. Below: every screen on its own, including Source Control's three tabs.
The rules this pass applied: one job per screen; one primary action per screen; no card inside a card; three type sizes (17 / 15 / 13) and the tiny monospace line only for a folder path.

Home (chosen: B, flattened)
Card = folder. Worktrees are rows: name left, ↑↓ and uncommitted right, chevron → Source Control. Agents indented under their worktree, unchanged from today. "New worktree" is the last row.

New worktree
Repository pre-filled from the card. Start from = the repo's default branch, changeable. Branch typed or from a GitHub issue. The sentence says exactly what will happen before it happens; one button.

Source Control — three tabs, one job each (Orca's structure), with what Orca's phone lacks in the header of every tab: the branch's ↑↓ vs main and the agent's status.
Changes: files with a stage checkbox and +/−; commit box pinned at the bottom with one button and "Let Claude write it".
Pull request: empty state says what creating will do (push first), one button, one text link.
Commits: ahead of main with Push; behind main with Pull main in. The ··· in the header holds Remove.

Remove
Names what would be lost and whether an agent is still working there. Safe path first; discard spelled out with counts; amber only on the safe action.

Considered and not chosen (owner pick 2026-09-02: B, one card per folder).
A — worktree is the card, branch first: Orca's model; loses the folder grouping, many cards per repo.
C — today's card with the branch on each agent row: smallest change; git state repeats per agent, a worktree with no agent has nowhere to appear, the line truncates.
